correctness.rationale: Exact generating-function extraction gives the coefficient recurrence. A Bernoulli-denominator bound shows the normalized polynomial summation operator preserves Z_2[x]. The normalized polynomial is x modulo 2^(nu2(m)) at all depths; convolution yields the exact claimed leading bit, with multiplier-one oddness showing sharpness. The standalone recurrence checker corroborates 500 finite cases and 40 sharp witnesses but infinite correctness follows from symbolic induction.

originality.rationale: The 2001 Rødseth–Sellers Theorem 1 and lemmas establish divisibility and extraction but not exact all-depth even-base sharpness or the normalized convolution; the full March 2024 Żmija article establishes general lower congruence moduli. The mathematically nearest full-text published studies respectively exclude even bases and fix the depth to three. No checked source states the same infinite targetwise even-base first-bit law, while unindexed or implicit coverage is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An implicit specialization of older high-order congruence machinery or an unindexed equivalent parity theorem cannot be excluded from published search alone.
The same extraction recurrence appears in prior work; the novel claim is the exact even-base leading-bit law, not the recurrence or universal lower bound.

value.rationale: The 2001 universal even-base congruence leaves the natural question of sharpness at all depths and its first nonzero binary digit. The theorem supplies an exact valuation family for every even base, every depth, and a stable parity profile at all multipliers; it is a structural, motivated sharpening with practical large-index reduction, not merely a small finite table or arbitrary slice.
